description: EOS 13-layer production stack design — desired end state, current state, gaps, and readiness

layers.desired_end_state: React 18 + Vite 5 + TypeScript + shadcn/ui + Tailwind CSS. Company/portfolio/workflow management dashboards. Responsive design. Dark mode. Component library aligned with OS Platform Standard v2.
layers.current_state: Two divergent implementations. GitHub main: 202 files, Replit-origin structure, basic React/Vite/TypeScript, shadcn/ui, Tailwind. Beast feature/company-system: 603 files, significantly expanded UI with company management, portfolio views, workflow pages. Beast frontend is more complete but unvalidated against main.
layers.gap: Source divergence is the primary gap. Beast has 3x the frontend code. No unified codebase exists. No component tests. No design system documentation.
dependencies: OS Platform Standard v2 design system
layers.shared_standard_applicability: React/Vite/TypeScript/shadcn/Tailwind from OS Platform Standard v2
layers.app_specific_notes: Beast branch has significantly more UI work. GitHub main is stale (last commit 2026-02-20, all Replit Agent authored). Cannot determine frontend quality without build validation on Beast.

layers.desired_end_state: Express 4 + TypeScript API server. RESTful endpoints for companies, portfolios, workflows, skills, agents, analytics. API versioning. Request validation. Typed request/response contracts.
layers.current_state: GitHub main: basic Express server with minimal routes. Beast: expanded Express server with company/portfolio/workflow/skill/agent routes. Drizzle ORM for database access. No API versioning. No formal request validation beyond basic TypeScript types.
layers.gap: Source divergence. No API documentation. No OpenAPI spec. No request validation middleware. No API versioning strategy. Beast routes unvalidated.
layers.shared_standard_applicability: Express/TypeScript/Drizzle from OS Platform Standard v2
layers.app_specific_notes: Beast has significantly more API routes covering company system, portfolio management, workflow execution. These routes need review and testing before promotion.

layers.desired_end_state: Neon Postgres. Drizzle ORM schema. Separate EOS database (not shared with other Trinity apps). Migrations managed via Drizzle. Schema covers: users, companies, portfolios, workflows, skills, agents, analytics, transactions, clients, offers.
layers.current_state: GitHub main: basic Drizzle schema with users, sessions. Beast: expanded schema with companies, portfolios, workflows, skills, agents. Both target Neon Postgres. No production database exists yet.
layers.gap: No production Neon database provisioned. Schema divergence between branches. No migration path defined. No backup strategy. No data seeding plan.
layers.shared_standard_applicability: Neon Postgres + Drizzle ORM from OS Platform Standard v2
layers.app_specific_notes: EOS needs its own Neon database, separate from CreatorOS and LyfeOS. Beast branch schema is more complete. Schema migration from chosen branch to production Neon is a future work packet.

layers.desired_end_state: Clerk authentication. Role-based access control. Session management via Clerk. OAuth providers (Google, GitHub). Organization/team support via Clerk organizations.
layers.current_state: GitHub main: Passport.js session-based auth (Replit origin). Beast feature/company-system: Clerk already integrated — has Clerk middleware, auth routes, session handling. Beast is ahead on auth.
layers.gap: GitHub main has legacy Passport.js auth that must be replaced. Beast has Clerk but it has not been end-to-end validated. Clerk configuration (API keys, org settings) not provisioned for production. No RBAC policy defined beyond basic auth.
layers.shared_standard_applicability: Clerk auth direction from OS Platform Standard v2
layers.app_specific_notes: If Beast branch is promoted (DEC-145-001 option A), Clerk auth is already partially integrated. If GitHub main is kept, full Clerk migration is required. Either path needs end-to-end auth validation.

layers.desired_end_state: Fly.io deployment. Dockerized application. Fly.toml configuration. Production environment variables. Health check endpoint. Zero-downtime deploys.
layers.current_state: No production deployment exists. No Fly.io configuration. No Dockerfile for production. No health check endpoint. Development only (local or Beast).
layers.gap: Complete gap — no deployment infrastructure exists. Requires Dockerfile, Fly.toml, environment configuration, health checks, and deployment pipeline.
layers.shared_standard_applicability: Fly.io deployment from OS Platform Standard v2
layers.app_specific_notes: EOS has no deployment history. First deployment will require full environment setup. VPS should not host EOS frontend — Fly.io is the target.

layers.desired_end_state: Fly.io for application hosting. Neon for managed Postgres. Clerk for managed auth. CDN for static assets. VPS (UMH) for orchestration only — not for serving EOS.
layers.current_state: No cloud compute provisioned for EOS. Development runs on Beast (Windows) locally. VPS runs UMH orchestration but does not serve EOS.
layers.gap: No cloud compute exists. All compute is local development on Beast. Production compute requires Fly.io provisioning.
layers.shared_standard_applicability: Fly.io + Neon + Clerk managed services from OS Platform Standard v2
layers.app_specific_notes: EOS compute is straightforward — single Fly machine for the Express/React app, Neon for database, Clerk for auth. No GPU or heavy compute requirements.

layers.desired_end_state: GitHub as version control. GitHub Actions for CI/CD. Automated build, test, lint on PR. Automated deployment to Fly.io on main merge. Branch protection on main.
layers.current_state: GitHub repo exists (antonyfmunoz/eos). No CI/CD pipeline. No GitHub Actions. No branch protection. No automated testing. Two divergent branches (main, feature/company-system on Beast).
layers.gap: Complete CI/CD gap. No automated pipeline. Branch strategy unresolved. No PR workflow. No automated deployment.
layers.shared_standard_applicability: GitHub + GitHub Actions from OS Platform Standard v2
layers.app_specific_notes: CI/CD cannot be implemented until source strategy is resolved and a test suite exists. Without tests, CI is just build verification.

layers.desired_end_state: RLS on all user-scoped tables. CSRF protection. XSS prevention (React default + CSP headers). SQL injection prevention (Drizzle parameterized queries). Secret management via environment variables. HTTPS enforced. Security headers.
layers.current_state: No RLS configured. Basic React XSS prevention. Drizzle provides parameterized queries. No CSP headers. No security headers. Secrets in .env files (not committed). HTTPS not applicable (no deployment).
layers.gap: No RLS. No security headers. No CSP. No security audit. No secret rotation policy. No vulnerability scanning.
layers.shared_standard_applicability: RLS + security headers from OS Platform Standard v2
layers.app_specific_notes: EOS will handle company/portfolio/financial data — RLS is mandatory. Multi-tenant data isolation required if EOS supports multiple organizations.

layers.desired_end_state: Rate limiting on all public API endpoints. Tiered limits by endpoint type (auth: strict, read: moderate, write: moderate, AI: strict). Rate limit headers in responses. Configurable per-tenant limits.
layers.current_state: No rate limiting exists. All endpoints are unprotected against abuse.
layers.gap: Complete gap. No rate limiting middleware. No limit configuration. No per-endpoint tuning.
dependencies: Deployment (rate limiting most critical in production)
layers.shared_standard_applicability: Rate limiting middleware from OS Platform Standard v2
layers.app_specific_notes: EOS may have AI-powered features (agent execution, skill recommendations) that require strict rate limiting to control cost.
validation_requirements: Rate limits enforced on auth endpoints

layers.desired_end_state: CDN for static frontend assets (Fly.io built-in or Cloudflare). API response caching for expensive queries. Browser caching headers for static assets. Redis or in-memory cache for hot data (optional, deferred).
layers.current_state: No CDN. No caching. No cache headers. Development only.
layers.gap: Complete gap. No caching strategy. No CDN configuration.
layers.shared_standard_applicability: CDN + caching strategy from OS Platform Standard v2
layers.app_specific_notes: EOS is a low-traffic application initially. CDN for static assets is sufficient. Redis caching is premature until traffic justifies it.

layers.desired_end_state: Fly.io auto-scaling (min 1, max 3 machines initially). Health check-based routing. Horizontal scaling capability. Database connection pooling via Neon.
layers.current_state: No scaling infrastructure. Single development instance.
layers.gap: Complete gap. No scaling configuration. No connection pooling.
layers.shared_standard_applicability: Fly.io scaling + Neon connection pooling from OS Platform Standard v2
layers.app_specific_notes: EOS is founder-use initially. Single machine is sufficient. Scaling configuration should be defined but aggressive scaling is premature.

layers.desired_end_state: Structured logging (JSON format). Error tracking service (Sentry or equivalent). PostHog for product analytics. Application logs accessible. Error alerting for critical failures.
layers.current_state: No structured logging. No error tracking. No PostHog. Console.log only in development.
layers.gap: Complete gap. No observability. No error tracking. No analytics.
layers.shared_standard_applicability: PostHog analytics + error tracking from OS Platform Standard v2
layers.app_specific_notes: EOS needs product analytics from day one of production. Error tracking is mandatory before production deployment. PostHog covers product analytics; need to determine if PostHog or a separate service covers error tracking.

layers.desired_end_state: Automated database backups (Neon built-in). Deployment rollback capability (Fly.io releases). Recovery runbook documented. RTO < 1 hour, RPO < 24 hours for initial launch. Uptime monitoring.
layers.current_state: No availability infrastructure. No backups. No rollback plan. No monitoring.
layers.gap: Complete gap. No recovery strategy. No backups. No monitoring.
layers.shared_standard_applicability: Neon backups + Fly.io rollback from OS Platform Standard v2
layers.app_specific_notes: Neon provides automatic backups. Fly.io provides release rollback. These are managed-service features that come with the platform choice. Recovery runbook is the main custom artifact needed.

summary.primary_blocker: EOS source strategy (DEC-145-001) must be resolved before any layer can proceed to implementation
